sources.note: 'Enwan is a stable indigenous language of Nigeria... Direct evidence is lacking'. No names, dialects, classification detail or resources on the free page.

sources.citation: Rolle, Nicholas. 2026. Tone diachrony beyond tonogenesis: Reconstructing the tone melodies of nouns in Proto-Edoid (Niger-Congo). lingbuzz/009572 v3, forthcoming in Diachronica.
sources.note: Footnote (txt lines 526-527): 'The Edoid languages not surveyed in this paper are Ikhin-Arokho [ikh], Enwan [env], Ikpeshi [ikp], Igwe [igw], Sasaru [sxs], Iyayu [iya], Akuku [ayk], and Okpe [okx]' -- confirms no tone-marked Enwan source was available to a 2026 family-wide tone survey. Nothing on stress for Enwan.

sources.citation: Ekwukoma, Victor & S. I. Odiagbe. 2025. A survey of language diversity and vitality in Edo State. JOLAN Supplement 5: 193-203. doi:10.60787/jolan.vol5no1.418
sources.note: Enwan listed among 26 languages of Edo State (Akoko-Edo LGA) and among the 'underdeveloped' ones with no orthography, literature or dictionary. No phonology.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Five Southern Northwestern Edoid Languages in Southern Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-012. SIL.
sources.note: Enwan [env] only in the glossary of neighbouring languages (fn.3: 'Not to be confused with Enwan [enw] spoken in Akwa Ibom state') and as a contact language of Akhukhu speakers. No Enwan data.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2021. Change Request Number 2021-019: adopted update [env] (2022-01-20). SIL International. (Glottolog ref 641373, one of the two refs for enwa1246)
sources.note: Name correction only: 'The State is incorrectly given as Edu instead of Edo' (p.2); submitted by Viamo Inc. staff on the basis of Wikipedia. No linguistic content.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 [ed. IV]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Entry 409 Sasaru-Enwan-Igwe: Edo State, Akoko-Edo LGA; 3,775 (1952); Edoid: North-Central Edoid ii; dialects Enwan, Igwe, Sasaru; 'Refs. Comparative: Elugbe (1989)' only -- no phonology or grammar reference exists.

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola. 2015. Deciphering Aborigines and Migrants from Cognation and Topography in North-Western Edo. Lengua y Migracion 7(1): 29-51.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Lexicostatistics only (pp.43-44, Table 5 'Cognation Percentages for Igwe Sale-Sasaru-Enwa'): 'there are no statistical bases for classifying Enwa as NCE, despite oral claims of their link with Emai, Sasaru and Igwe Sale'; Enwa-Sasaru c.60%, Enwa-Igwe c.50%, Enwa-North Ibie 68%, Enwa-Atte 67%, Enwa-Okpe 67%, Enwa-Akuku 60%; 'Enwa originally belonged to the eastern borders of Akoko-Edo'. Draws on Lewis 2013.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid enwa1246 and reference record 550315 (Lewis, Ademola Anthony. 2013. North Edoid relations and roots. PhD, University of Ibadan, xvi+327 pp.)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. enwa1246 MED = 'wordlist_or_less' from the ISO change request and Ethnologue; no descriptive reference. Lewis 2013 (hhtype overview;comparative;wordlist) has an lgcode list of 16 varieties that does NOT include Enwan [env], although Lewis 2015 reports Enwa cognate counts from the same thesis.

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Enwan appears only as a one-village community (p.68-69), in the mutual-intelligibility group 'Atte Ikpeshi-Enwan-Okpilla-North Ibie (NWE)' (p.69), among languages Elugbe left unclassified, and among villages where narrative tapes were recorded. Table 8 'Linguistic Features of NCE and NWE' (tones 2 / 2+DS / 3) has no Enwan row. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America. (Zenodo 5618102)
sources.note: Classification list only; sec. 13.3.4 'Tone systems' (pp.298-299) surveys Degema, Egene, Eruwa, Isoko, Edo, Ghotuo, Oloma, Ibilo, Emhalhe -- no Enwan, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press. xvii+253 pp. (Zenodo 5688969, CC-BY)
sources.note: Nothing for Enwan. Enwan is named only on pp.10-11 ('Ikpeshi, Sasaru, and Enwan, all of Akoko-Edo' among clans 'most likely North-Central Edoid peoples'), pp.11-12 ('Igarra... is actually contiguous with Enwan (NCE) and Enwan is in turn only a couple of miles from Akuku, a NWE village') and in the classification list p.24 '(h) Igwe-Enwa-Sasaru', with the footnote that g-i 'are left out of the family tree because their exact relationship with the rest of NCE has not been determined'. No Enwan sketch, no Enwan forms in the lexicon (Glottolog langnote: 'Mentions... Enwan (Edu State) [env]... but…

sources.citation: Joshua Project language page env; en.wikipedia 'Enwan language' and 'Edoid languages'; edoworld.net Akoko-Edo history pages; ISO 639-3 code page env
sources.note: Nothing. Joshua Project: alternate names Enwa, Enwan; Bible portions 2024; GRN audio and Jesus Film exist. Wikipedia 'Edoid languages' comparative vocabulary table from Lewis (2013) has no Enwa row (Ghotuo, Sasaru, Ikhin, Arokho, Uroe, Igwe Sale/Oke, Ake, Okpuje, Sobongida only); Lewis (2013:160) classification groups Enwa with Atte and Ikpeshi. edoworld: 'Eight distinct languages... Ojiramis (Group II) understand... Enwan (Group I)', migration history only.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2025. Edoid: Tone in Affirmative and Negative Declarative Clauses. In Springer handbook (ch. 23).

sources.citation: Lewis, Ademola Anthony. 2013. North Edoid relations and roots. PhD dissertation, University of Ibadan. xvi+327 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only work with first-hand Enwa data (tone-marked comparative wordlists; Enwa cognate percentages in Lewis 2015 come from it; Lewis 2013:160 classifies Enwa with Atte and Ikpeshi). May contain tone-marked Enwa forms and a note on the tone system; a stress statement is unlikely but this is the only place one could exist.
